rationale: Two scenes share a shape. In 31:32 Jacob, accused of theft, says, 'If you find your gods with anyone here, he shall not live!', and the narrator adds, 'For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols'; Laban then searches tent by tent (31:33-35). In 44:9 Jacob's sons, accused of theft, say, 'If any of your servants is found to have it, he must die'; the steward searches 'beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest', and 'the cup was found in Benjamin's sack' (44:12, BSB). Benjamin is Rachel's son. The BSB's English differs, and so does the Hebrew of the penalty: Bible Hub's interlinear shows lo yichyeh ('he shall not live', Strong's 2421) in 31:32 and va-met ('then he shall die', Strong's 4191) in 44:9, though both oaths are built on the verb matsa, 'find' (Strong's 4672). Matthew Michael (Journal for Semitics, 2018) reports Gordon Wenham's comment that 'the search for Laban's teraphim has similarities with the search for Joseph's cup (44:1-3)' and Meir Sternberg's reading of the brothers' answer against 'Jacob's hyperbolic outburst' in 31:32; both are read here only through Michael. Graded motif at plausible, following conn-gen20-righteous-gen18, because the shared elements are checkable in the text but the link is a reader's, the wording of the penalty differs, and Genesis 44 does not refer back to Genesis 31.
